title: underworld business practices
content:
from my podcast: botanical studies of internet magic
listen on spotify / listen on apple

the vast majority of business advice has never worked for me, not because it was wrong, but because it didn't align with my energy, and the way I wanted to exist in the world. it took me years to build my own operating system -- a model for business that didn't make me want to burn it all down, ghost everything, and just get a day job.

I realized that I run my business like a super scorpio -- lunar, cyclical, waiting behind veils, operating from the depths. Far from being a weakness, that it's my greatest power. I'm calling this my"underworld business practices" -- and today, I've distilled them down into 8 parts to share with you.

Hi friends, this is Botanical Studies of Internet Magic, a podcast on the alchemy of creative power through the vessel and portal of the internet. My name is Kening and I'll be your guide.

on running a business like a scorpio

In the last couple of months, I was reflecting on the way that I run my creative business. And I realized that without even intending to, I run my business very much like a Scorpio stellium that I am. It just kind of happened over these last many years of rejecting traditional business advice and leaning into what felt good, natural, and energetically sustainable for my system.

Typically, when I look at the business advice out there, how we're taught to do business is around emphasizing consistency, visibility, transparency, capturing and maintaining attention in your audience, networking, outreach, building relationships, trying to be more inclusive and get attention and boost engagement. But for me, none of that really worked. And all of that just sounded really exhausting, not to mention a little bit boring. I need to do things for my business that keep me engaged.

So you could call me antisocial for sure, but I'd rather have one intense conversation than 10 superficial ones. I'd rather be the cult leader of a secret society than a pop star loved by billions. And I think that the ways in which I do business and I create on the internet is through density and intensity.

It took me a really long time to feel like I had permission to show up as that in the sort of kaleidoscopic, multidimensional too muchness of who I am. And eventually I realized that this is my power to inhabit and share in the abundance of my underworld. And so this podcast is about that.

Most business advice wasn't created for people that feel like me. And today I wanted to articulate and distill down eight practices and principles for how I run my business like a super Scorpio, like a lunar goddess, high priestess, hermit, queen of the underworld. And as I'm saying this, I'm kind of embarrassed, like, oh my God, is that how I think about myself? And it's not how I think about myself, but maybe it could be in order to claim the power that I feel within.

the eight practices

So I will list the eight key practices as single words right here, and then I'll go through them one by one in more depth.

Number one is power. Number two is repelling. Number three is waiting. Number four is clarity. Number five is obsession. Number six is cyclical. Number seven is mystery. Number eight is void.

If you're curious about working deeper with me around building creative businesses, I'm currently plotting a new course for 2026 called Digital Abundance. And it's about transforming, channeling, and metabolizing inner creative abundance to material wealth. And you can take a peek in the show notes.

1. power — cultivating inner abundance

In our eight underworld business practices, practice one is power, cultivating your personal power as inner abundance.

I've had many definitions of what power means to me, but the one that keeps coming back to me again and again is this: power is having everything to give and needing nothing in return. Power is about knowing and centering in your own abundance, cultivating it like a garden, standing firmly in it and believing in it. So in that sense, power is feeling infinity, feeling the opposite of scarcity, feeling that you have more than enough.

Where do you feel abundance in your life? Where does your sense of inner abundance live in your creative body? For me, I feel abundant in ideas, in inner visions, in imagination, in ways of seeing the world, in emotions, dreams, sensitivity, creative possibilities. And I metabolize and share that abundance in my digital ecosystem as art, writings, podcast episodes, offerings, things that now exist independent of me.

From the outside, I think it comes off as generosity that I'm sharing my abundance, but internally, honestly, I just experience it as tending to my empress garden and allowing it to exist and be shared without expecting anything in return.

I started with this practice because I think it is the underlying belief, assumption, and practice that feeds everything else that you create in your business ecosystem. When you have a clear sense of where your power lives and you tend to it every day, you work with it, be in conversation with it, then there's nothing that can really shake you.

Your sense of power doesn't live in your bank account and doesn't live in your followers list or on any platform. Those things can ebb and flow. Your sense of power lives in a place that is infinitely replenishable by you. It lives in your relationship to your creativity and your relationship to yourself.

2. repelling — boundaries as protection

Practice two is repelling. So repelling as in repelling spells, protecting your boundaries, and embrace and celebrate the fact that you are not for everyone.

So in order to be magnetizing to the right people, you have to be repelling to the wrong people. If business practices of the solar world is about saying yes to people and showing them how you can serve them, then the business practice of the underworld is about saying no, saying no to the wrong people so that they can bounce off the page.

And I don't mean repelling in a sort of offensive way or like a stinky skunk kind of way. I mostly mean having crystal clear boundaries in the way that you do your work and share your work so that the wrong people will not be attracted to it.

For example, I know that my work can be pretty dense and internal, and I don't try to be more digestible and palatable to the general audience. I practice clarity and confidence knowing that my work is not for them. It's kind of like before you do witchcraft of any sort, you need to draw a circle, create a boundary around the ritual to protect and contain what happens inside of it. It's being so clear in the belief that if they don't like this, then they can leave. I don't need everyone to like me.

So another concrete example, there's an exercise I teach inside my course sharing space camp called the repelling exercise in which you identify what it is you're afraid of coming off as, and then you practice doing exactly that. It's basically uncensoring yourself from being fully yourself. So think about what internalized dialogue you have in your mind about what you're too much of—too emotional, too chaotic, too crazy, too what—and then practice doing that, letting it rub people the wrong way because when you repel the wrong people, you attract the right people to you.

Once I've embraced this part of my underworld business practice, I've learned to feel relief and even a kind of pleasure when people unsubscribe from my newsletter. It's like the wrong people leaving your house party. Having someone in your house or in your newsletter or on your website, it's an intimate experience, it's an intimate place. So you want to make it easy for them to leave. You want to make it clear that it's not for them. And the way you do it is simply by being uncompromisingly yourself.

3. waiting — the power of patience

Underworld practice three: waiting. Waiting for the right people to come to you on their own time.

The principle here is to never chase. Never chase clients, audience, or your community. Always wait for them to come to you. And I don't mean like to be unavailable, but the first contact, the first way in which they wander into your world, make their way into your cave, make that pathway easy and clear for them to find you at the same time, make it specific.

And this is not about being hard to get or hard to reach or exclusive, quote unquote. This is about standing so firmly in your power and trusting that the right people will wander in on their own time. This is why I don't create any kind of false urgency in my marketing practices. It doesn't feel genuine to me. And I want people to want the thing that I'm offering on their own terms because their attraction to the work I'm doing will make them a better fit. And ultimately both of us would have a better experience.

I let them to filter themselves and decide if they're the right fit. And so concretely, when I design offerings, I don't try to make it super digestible or generic or understandable for everyone. I make it as specific as possible. And I do this just by using my own voice, practicing, talking about the offering, the way that I would talk about it to my past self. I find that speaking to a multidimensional human being, whether that's yourself or someone in your community, makes it feel a lot more living and fleshy instead of imagining this like cardboard customer avatar.

When it comes to the principle of waiting, I think I have to mention also in human design, I'm a projector. So my strategy is to wait for the invitation. Waiting sometimes seems like it's passive, like there's a lack of agency in waiting, but I wanna reframe this and say that waiting is power. Waiting is to practice conservation of energy so that you can focus on your inner and creative resources. While you wait, you focus on cultivating your abundance.

A concrete example of this is my philosophy of digital world building, which is the strategy of waiting. I create and share my ideas, writing art on my website for people to come visit and be a part of and wander through. I wait for the right people to spend time there. I create offerings in alignment with that abundance. And then oftentimes once I've released those offerings, people sign up for them who have been following me and visiting my world for years. It's like we waited for each other in the dark and trusted in the right moment to come together.

And I will say as a side note, my approach to waiting is a lot slower. I'm sure that I miss out on additional sales, but as a result, I think I also filter only the ones who are truly resonant with my offering will sign up for it.

4. clarity — commitment to truth

Underworld business practice four: clarity as commitment to truth.

Whenever I design any kind of offering or even write or create anything for my world, I think about what is at the heart and soul of this thing. What is it really about? And this requires going deep and investigating as to what is my motivation for creating this? What makes us come alive? What makes me feel alive when I work with this?

Because I think anything we create in our business ecosystem is a sort of creative conversation, is a channeling between your life experiences, the intuitive spirit world and what we metabolize and create. Finding clarity is that piece which helps all the other puzzle pieces come together. It's starting with the heart and blood of the body and moving outwards from there.

I find that a lot of times when designing a business offering, it can be really easy to get caught up in the nuts and bolts of timing—should this be seasonal? Should this be ongoing? How much should it cost? The sort of logistics around the shape and form of the business container. But focusing on clarity first is to focus on the pumping heart and blood of this offering. What is it really about? What makes it come alive?

And when you start there, it allows you to create the shape to serve its sense of aliveness rather than the other way around. Creating an offering from that deep clarity feels much easier because you've already animated the body of this offering and then you can decide how you want it to move.

And I think it's this crucial ingredient of clarity that allows me to be both repelling and magnetizing at the same time.

For more of my reflections on cultivating clarity, which can feel like such an elusive thing, you can listen to episode 20, clarity is a bird I follow home. And the questions I ask there are: What do I deeply desire? What do I hope to create? How do I want this to feel? The more that I'm clear on my motivations for creating something, for launching a course or a new offering, the more that I'm connected to my clarity for why this needs to exist, the more potent my projection and magnetic field for this offering.

I've allowed a sense of clarity to metabolize for many, many months until it becomes a guiding light for how I create, design and release it.

5. obsession — channeling intensity

Underworld Business Practice 5: obsession, all or nothingness.

The quality of being obsessed with something can feel like having tunnel vision, like you're totally immersed underwater, a sort of self-suffocation and extreme density. Typically, we think of obsession as being a little bit unbalanced or feeling unreliable when it comes to building a sustainable business ecosystem. It feels like having a fever or being one of the obscurus in fantastic beasts. It's all consuming and even a bit destructive.

I get obsessed whenever I teach any new course. It's like all I can think about with 99.9% of my brain, even when I'm recording a podcast episode or writing something, it's like a mini obsessive sprint for me in which nothing else exists.

I actually think that being too balanced can be overrated. If you're the kind of person that gets swept up in obsessive energy, you can use that. You can channel that as a sort of magical, powerful, creative force through creating clear containers and boundaries, through designing systems and practices to serve your obsession by giving it a transition ritual, by giving it clear beginnings and endings, by keeping a pulse on the things you're obsessed with and using that. It's like a force of nature, turning that into an offering or a creation of some sort.

I think that being obsessive can get a bad reputation in which you are negligent of the other aspects of your business. And it's definitely a thing that I experience each time I come out of a sort of immersive, creative sprint. I get anxious and I worry about: did I let the other balls of my business and life drop? What did I forget to take care of? This is why having clear systems and minimalist housekeeping to-do lists can ground you as you move in and out of your obsessive containers. The key here is to create those containers for generative obsession, energy that can be metabolized into creativity and abundance.

6. cyclical — rhythmic ebb and flow

Underworld practice number six is cyclical energy. This is the practice of aligning the tidal ebb and flow of your energy with your creative and business rhythms.

We live in a world that is ruled by the tyranny of the daily streak and the sort of fixation on linear measurable progress. We're taught that to be steady and consistent and reliable is more holy than being in cyclical seasonal patterns. I don't think it's an either or. Sometimes you need the grounding anchoring practice of a daily ritual. And sometimes you need sudden disruption and energizing change like an obsessive sprint. What's crucial here is discerning what your energy needs to observe your natural ebb and flow.

Instead of forcing yourself to be consistent, what if you embraced the extremes of your cycles? Instead of pushing yourself to show up every day, what if you gave yourself permission to disappear and reappear? Instead of forcing steady output, what if you created spaciousness to hibernate? Instead of trying to pace yourself all the time, what if you went all out intensity and nothingness?

I think what's crucial here is that you create boundaries that allow you to move through a single cycle where you have the wintering disappearance as well as the spring re-emergence. Working with cyclical energy and cyclical patterns can feel a little more complicated than forcing yourself to show up every day. But when you really inhabit it, you also experience the magic of elastic time and potential.

Becoming your own master of time is not about trying to control it, dominate it, colonize it, parcel it out in tiny sugar cubes. Instead, it's about riding time and energy like a tsunami wave. So that's being extremely discerning and in touch with knowing when you need to go underwater and when you need to resurface again.

And this may or may not be visible from the outside. As a concrete example, recently I've been working on cultivating more consistency in my digital ecosystem of sending newsletters and podcast episodes, but I've done it through embracing my non-linear intense cycles of creation and building in buffer time. I allow myself to be cyclical when I create and more consistent when I share.

After the release of any new offering, I make sure to build in nothingness time where I can hibernate and be in my winter season and emerge when I feel ready to emerge. Cyclical business energy practices is the way to make this work feel sustainable, nourishing and generative. As a result, I actually feel like my capacity and creative output is greater in so much more magnitude because I'm not constantly struggling against burnout.

7. mystery — love affair with the unknown

Underworld business practice number seven is mystery. Having a love affair with the unknown.

I've never actually tried to cultivate an aura of mystery around my work, but I've had many students and people sign up for my courses and offerings saying that they don't quite get what it is exactly. They understand the essence of the thing. They are resonant with my philosophy. They trust me and my work. They're drawn inwards by the intrigue. And so the clarity isn't in the nuts and bolts of what I'm sharing or teaching. It's in the heart ethos with which I move through the world.

For me, I think I create with a sense of mystery because being in conversation with the unknown is what keeps me feeling excited and interested in my work to keep working. So much that I've structured and themed my seasonal community, Labyrinth Library, around the practice of moving through the unknown.

I translate this devotion to mystery as a desire to constantly experiment, play, do deep inquiry work, explore possibilities, adventure, and to be curious about building and trying new things. Most courses that I teach feel like I'm riding this edge between what I know and have deeply embodied for many years and new insights and frameworks and processes that I'm discovering along with my students.

I think it's because I'm so comfortable at the edge of what I don't know that is what makes my work feel alive and have a spark of mystery and intrigue to me. It's what gives it a sense of magic and possibility because I never frame or position myself as the person who has all the answers. I think of myself as an expedition guide in which we discover something together. It's the transformative experience that we will have together that is the heart and soul of the work.

8. void — tenacity in the dark

Number eight of my underworld business practices is the void: tenacity in the dark.

The void is the space of nothingness, of the liminal in between here and there. If mystery is about being in conversation with the unknown, then the void is about allowing yourself to be annihilated by the unknown.

It's the feeling of writing and sharing in your website when you're not sure if anyone will ever read it. It's sending a newsletter and getting no responses. It's the sound of silence. It's the texture of darkness. It's a womb-like space when everything feels terrifying, meaningless, and yet also cocooning and possible. It's the possibility of ego death, insignificance, annihilation.

It's saying and believing that even if no one ever sees your work, no one ever sees your art, it is still worth making and releasing into the world.

I talk about the void in detail in week one of my course, "Sharing Space Camp," in which I frame the digital universe as the void. The internet is the void. But also whenever I'm feeling a bit existential, I'm very aware of the fact that we are creating all of these things, releasing it into the ethereal space, that everything is dust anyway. We're going to die anyway. And this can feel very dark and depressing, or it can feel empowering and freeing.

If there is only void in this world, if we are already here and gone again, then what is it that stops me from committing a thousand percent to that which makes me feel alive, to survive the abyss and share the jewels that we've uncovered in the darkness?

To be tenacious in the dark nothingness of the void is to be comfortable with death, to have nothing to lose, and therefore to have everything to give.

in closing

In closing, today I've shared eight of my underworld business practices.

The first is power, cultivating your inner abundance as your greatest source of power.

The second is repelling, boundaries that repel to protect your magic circle.

The third is waiting for the right people to wander into your cave on their own time.

The fourth is clarity, commitment to your deepest motivation and truth.

The fifth is obsession, channeling obsession as a chaotic, powerful creative force.

The sixth is cyclical, working in rhythmic ebb and flow with your energy.

The seventh is mystery, embracing your love affair with the unknown.

And the eighth is void, transcending a fear of death.

For me, these practices and principles have shown me that there is a space for a radically different way of creating, sharing and building a business on the internet—a way that allows us to celebrate our strengths instead of thinking we need to become someone or something else. This is by no means an exhaustive list. Articulating it has helped me feel more committed to the power that I see in this work. And I'm super excited to keep venturing deeper into the underworld and discovering what else is possible.

Thank you friends for listening to this episode. I'm teaching a new course called Digital Abundance. You can look at the invitations page in the show notes. I also lead a seasonal community and guidance vessel called Labyrinth Library, which you can sign up for in the show notes. The best way to keep in touch with me is through my newsletter. You can also explore more of my work and creative courses on my website and learn more about working with me one-on-one through a three month advising container called Liminal Leap. Until next time, take care.
